jurisdiction.name: Indonesia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Indonesia steers AI mainly through soft law: the National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2020-2045, the communications ministry's 2023 circular on AI ethics, and the financial services authority's (OJK) AI ethics guides for fintech and banking. Its binding AI-relevant rules are the 2022 Personal Data Protection Law and a 2026 health ministry decree on AI-based medical devices. A March 2026 joint decree by seven ministers sets rules for using and teaching AI in education, while Presidential Regulations on an AI roadmap and AI ethics were still awaiting signature.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs (Komdigi)
narrative.review_notes: This review was first completed on 12 October 2026 and redone in a longer pass on 13 October 2026, covering the ministries' legal databases, Parliament, the government, each ministry and each sector regulator. Not yet verified from the official text: material on the national regulations database, Parliament's legislation programme and the websites of the Supreme Court, cyber agency, competition authority and standards body. The two AI Presidential Regulations, the data protection law's 2026 implementing regulation and an updated OJK ethics guide are tracked as leads.

instruments.english_title: Circular of the Minister of Communication and Informatics No. 9 of 2023 on Artificial Intelligence Ethics
instruments.issuing_authority: Minister of Communication and Informatics (now Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs)
instruments.current_status: Set and promulgated in Jakarta on 19 December 2023 (JDIH Komdigi record). Still the ministry's operative AI-ethics instrument in October 2026: Komdigi's 2025 Concept AI Ethics Guideline was developed to strengthen it, and a Presidential Regulation on AI Ethics was awaiting the President's signature (see leads).
instruments.summary: Ministerial circular addressed to businesses carrying out AI-based programming (KBLI 62015) and to public- and private-scope electronic system operators, giving ethical values and principles for AI consultation, analysis and programming. It serves as the ethics reference for the internal AI data and ethics policies that Ministerial Regulation 3/2021 already requires of such businesses, and sets out values (inclusivity, humanity, security, accessibility, transparency, credibility and accountability, personal data protection, sustainable development, intellectual property) and responsibilities, including that AI must not be operated as the determinant of policy or decisions concerning humanity and that providers must prevent racism and other harms.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Indonesia's first national AI ethics instrument; the main AI-specific government text in force.

instruments.english_title: Law of the Republic of Indonesia No. 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Indonesia with the approval of the House of Representatives (DPR)
instruments.current_status: Enacted and promulgated 17 October 2022 (State Gazette 2022 No. 196, Supplement No. 6820); in force from promulgation, with a two-year adjustment period for controllers. Not yet verified from the official text: an implementing Government Regulation (PP 33/2026, set 16 July 2026 and applying from 16 January 2027) (see leads).
instruments.summary: Indonesia's general personal data protection law, binding on public and private controllers and processors. Art. 10 gives data subjects the right to object to decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that have legal effects or significant impact on them, with procedures to be set by Government Regulation; Art. 34(2)(a) lists automated decision-making with legal or significant effects among high-risk processing that requires a data protection impact assessment.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rules on automated decision-making and profiling that apply to AI systems processing personal data.

instruments.english_title: Indonesia National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2020-2045 (Stranas KA)
instruments.issuing_authority: Agency for the Assessment and Application of Technology (BPPT), working group on the national AI strategy (BPPT is now part of BRIN)
instruments.current_status: First printed December 2020 by BPPT Press (foreword dated July 2020); BPPT has since been merged into BRIN, whose repository hosts the full text. It was not given legal force; Komdigi states the draft Presidential Regulation on the National AI Roadmap 2026-2029 is being prepared together with the Stranas KA, and that regulation was still unsigned in October 2026 (see leads).
instruments.summary: Long-term national AI strategy drafted by a BPPT-convened quadruple-helix working group as the reference for ministries, agencies, regional governments and other stakeholders. Across eight chapters it sets a vision to 2045, a chapter on AI ethics and policy, focus areas (ethics and policy, talent, infrastructure and data, industrial research and innovation) and five priority sectors: health services, bureaucratic reform, education and research, food security, and mobility and smart cities.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Indonesia's only published national AI strategy.

instruments.issuing_authority: Financial Services Authority (OJK) with the fintech associations AFTECH, AFSI, AFPI and ALUDI
instruments.current_status: Posted on OJK's publication pages on 4 December 2023. A guide, not an OJK regulation (POJK).
instruments.summary: Code-of-conduct guide issued by OJK with four fintech associations for fintech operators that develop or use AI. It sets four basic principles (beneficial; fair and accountable; transparent and explicable; robust and secure), drawing on the OECD AI Principles and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and describes expectations such as non-discrimination, consumer protection, data protection, human oversight and robustness testing across operators' AI-based business models.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First financial-sector AI ethics guidance in Indonesia.

instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence Governance for Indonesian Banking
instruments.current_status: Published on OJK's banking roadmap and guidelines page on 29 April 2025 as a guide for banks; it complements POJK 11/POJK.03/2022 on bank IT operations and the Digital Banking Transformation Blueprint. The document is bilingual (Indonesian and English).
instruments.summary: OJK guide for banks in Indonesia to develop and deploy AI, including advanced, generative and agentic AI systems, responsibly. Its chapters cover AI risks and challenges (including deepfakes and GenAI risks), a benchmark of AI regulation in other countries, guiding principles for responsible and trustworthy AI, AI risk management and governance with risk classification of AI systems, implementation steps for high-risk AI, and supervision and AI audit (using frameworks such as NIST AI RMF, COBIT, ISACA and IIA).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main banking-sector AI governance and risk-management reference from the financial supervisor.

instruments.english_title: Decree of the Minister of Health No. HK.01.07/MENKES/951/2026 on Guidelines for Marketing Authorisation of Software-Based Medical Devices
instruments.current_status: Set in Jakarta on 7 September 2026 and in force from that date (fourth dictum); listed as 'Berlaku' (in force) on JDIH Kemenkes.
instruments.summary: Ministerial decree setting the guideline the Ministry of Health applies when granting marketing authorisation (izin edar) for software-based medical devices: Software as a Medical Device, Software in a Medical Device and medical devices with AI applications, including machine-learning and generative models. It sets dossier content on the AI model and its training, requires local clinical validation in Indonesia for certain imported software (retrained on Indonesian data, or using moderate- to high-risk AI for diagnosis, screening or clinical decisions), and requires a new authorisation for changes affecting intended use, main function or clinical performance.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First binding sector rule in Indonesia with specific requirements for AI-enabled products (health).

instruments.english_title: Joint Decree of the Ministers of Home Affairs, Religious Affairs, Primary and Secondary Education, Higher Education, Science and Technology, Communication and Digital Affairs, Population and Family Development, and Women's Empowerment and Child Protection on Guidelines for the Use and Learning of Digital Technology and Artificial Intelligence in Formal, Non-formal and Informal Education
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministers of Home Affairs; Religious Affairs; Primary and Secondary Education; Higher Education, Science and Technology; Communication and Digital Affairs; Population and Family Development (Head of BKKBN); Women's Empowerment and Child Protection (joint decree)
instruments.current_status: Set in Jakarta on 12 March 2026 and in force from that date (dictum KEDELAPAN). Numbered separately by each of the seven ministries (Komdigi's number is Kepmen 117/2026, listed as 'Berlaku' on JDIH Komdigi); posted by the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education on 16 March 2026. Implementation is coordinated by the Coordinating Ministry for Human Development and Culture, to which the ministries report every six months (dicta KELIMA-KEENAM).
instruments.summary: Joint decree of seven ministers setting national guidelines for using and teaching digital technology and AI across formal, non-formal and informal education, built on human-centred, child-protection and ethics principles. Education units are to assess readiness (data management, academic and AI ethics, digital literacy), apply the annexed guidelines and protect children from online harms; the annex sets level-specific rules, e.g. no direct interaction with AI platforms for early-childhood learners, only teacher-guided group use in primary school, a 'red zone' banning AI in exams and graded tasks, AI-plagiarism and personal-data rules for pupils, and principles, risk mitigation and AI governance for higher education. Each ministry's role (including Komdigi on platform safety) is set out, with six-monthly reporting.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First national, cross-ministry instrument specifically governing AI use (including generative AI) in education.

organizations.name: Ministry of Health
organizations.ai_governance_role: Kementerian Kesehatan; issued Decree HK.01.07/MENKES/951/2026 on marketing authorisation of software-based medical devices, including AI-enabled devices.

organizations.name: House of Representatives of the Republic of Indonesia
organizations.ai_governance_role: Dewan Perwakilan Rakyat (DPR); enacts laws jointly with the President, including Law 27/2022 on Personal Data Protection.

organizations.name: Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education
organizations.ai_governance_role: Kementerian Pendidikan Dasar dan Menengah (Kemendikdasmen); co-signatory and publisher of the 2026 seven-minister joint decree on digital technology and AI in education; runs the Coding and AI elective in schools.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National sources in Indonesia were searched, including legal databases, parliament, the communications and digital ministry, each ministry and each sector regulator. No qualifying material was found for procurement, cyber-security, transparency, standards, sandboxes, readiness indexes, international instruments or historical documents. Several official sites, including the main legal databases, parliament, the cyber agency, the standards body and the press council, were unavailable, so items such as the 2026 data protection implementing regulation and the presidential regulations on AI remain leads to check.
